title: Neural Network Basics: Understanding Activation Functions in Deep Learning

cues.en: Instructor: Hello and welcome back to the course on deep learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到深度學習。

cues.en: All right, today we're talking about the activation function.
Let's get straight into it.
So this is where we left off previously.
We talked about the structure of a one neuron.
So there it is in the middle.
We know that it has some inputs, values coming in.
It's got some weights.
Then it adds up the weighted, it calculates the weighted some of those inputs, and then applies the activation function.
cues.zh: 計算輸入加權和，再套活化函數。

cues.en: And on step three, it passes on the signal to the next neuron.
cues.zh: 第三步傳給下一神經元。

cues.en: And that's what we're talking about today.
We're talking about the value that is going to be passed over.
So we're talking about the activation function that's being applied.
cues.zh: 也就是套用的活化函數。

cues.en: So what options do we have for the activation function?
Well, we're going to look at four different types of activation functions that you can choose from.
Of course, there are more different types of activation functions, but these are the predominant ones that you'll be hearing about and that we'll be using in this course.
cues.zh: 當然更多，但這幾個最主要，常聽、本課會用。

cues.en: So here is the threshold function.
This is what it looks like.
So on the X-axis you have the weighted sum of inputs.
On the Y-axis, you have just, you know the values from zero to one.
And basically the threshold function is a very simple type of function where if the value is less than zero,
then the threshold function passes on zero.
If the value is more than zero or equal to zero, then threshold function passes on a one.
So it's basically kind of like a yes, no type of function.
Very, very straightforward, very kind of like rigid type of function.
Either yes or no, no other options.
So there you go. That's how it works.
A very simple function.
Let's move on to something a bit more complex now.
The sigmoid function, a very interesting formula that we have here, you'll see it just now.
There it is. One divided by one plus e to the power of -x.
cues.zh: 1 除以 1 加 e 的 −x 次方。

cues.en: Whereas in this case, of course, x is the value of the weighted sums.
cues.zh: 這裡 x 當然是加權和。

cues.en: And so yeah, so this is what the sigmoid looks like.
It's a function which is used in the logistic regression, if you recall, from the machine learning course.
cues.zh: 機器學習課的邏輯斯迴歸用它，記得嗎？

cues.en: So what is good about this function is that it is smooth.
Unlike the threshold function, this one doesn't have those kinks in its curve, and therefore it's just nice and smooth, gradual progression.
cues.zh: 不像閾值，曲線沒折角，平順、漸進。

cues.en: So anything below zero, it just like drops off, above zero, it
cues.zh: 小於 0 逐漸下降，大於 0

cues.en: approximates towards one.
And this sigmoid function is very useful in the final layer, in the output layer, especially when you are trying to predict probabilities.
cues.zh: 最後輸出層很有用，尤其預測機率。

cues.en: And we'll see that throughout this course.
And then we've got the rectifier function.
The rectifier function, even though it has a kink, is one of the most popular functions for artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 雖有折角，仍是 ANN 最熱門之一。

cues.en: So it goes all the way to zero, it is zero.
And then from there, it gradually progresses as the input value increases as well.
cues.zh: 之後隨輸入增加而增加。

cues.en: And we'll see that throughout the course.
We'll see that in other in tuition tutorials, and we'll also see that, how we use this function in the practical side of the course.
cues.zh: 其他概念課、實作也會看到用法。

cues.en: And I will comment on this a bit more in a few slides from now.
So just remember that a rectifier function is one of the most used functions in artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 記得整流函數是 ANN 最常用之一。

cues.en: And finally, we've got one more function that you will probably hear about.
cues.zh: 最後另一個可能聽到的。

cues.en: It's the hyperbolic tangent function.
It's very similar to the sigmoid function, but here the hyperbolic tangent function goes below zero.
So the values go from zero to one or approximate to one and go from zero to minus one on the other side.
cues.zh: 一側從 0 到或漸近 1，另一側從 0 到 −1。

cues.en: And that can be useful in some applications.
So we're not going to go into too much depth on each one of these functions.
I just wanted to acquaint you of them so that you know what they look like and what they're called.
If you'd like to get some additional reading, then check out this paper by Xavier Glorot,
cues.zh: 想延伸讀，Xavier Glorot 的論文，

cues.en: Xavier Glorot, called Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks, 2011 paper.
cues.zh: 2011 年 Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks。

cues.en: And there you will find out exactly why the rectifier function is such a valuable function, why it's so popularly used.
cues.zh: 可知道整流函數為何有價值、如此普及。

cues.en: But nevertheless, for now, you don't really need to know all of those things.
For now, we're just going to start applying them.
We'll just start using them more and more and more.
And so when you feel comfortable with the practical side of things, then you can go and refer to this paper, and then you'll be able to soak in that knowledge
cues.zh: 實作熟悉後，再看論文，吸收

cues.en: much quicker and it'll make much more sense.
So, but just keep this in mind that when you're ready, when you feel that you're ready, then you can go and refer to this paper and get some valuable knowledge from there.
cues.zh: 記得準備好再參考，取得有用知識。

cues.en: So just to quickly recap, we have the threshold activation function, which looks like this, the sigmoid activation function, which looks like this.
cues.zh: 快速回顧，閾值長這樣，Sigmoid 長這樣。

cues.en: We have the rectifier function and we have the hyperbolic tangent function.
And now to finish off this tutorial, let's quickly do a few exercises.
So we'll just do two quick exercises to help that knowledge sink in.
So first one is we've got an example here of a neural network with just one neuron, and then right away the output layer.
cues.zh: 先看只有一神經元、接著輸出層的例子。

cues.en: And the question is, assuming that your dependent variable is binary, so it's either zero or one, which threshold function would you use?
cues.zh: 假設應變數二元，0 或 1，會選哪個活化函數？

cues.en: So out of the ones that we've discussed, we have the threshold function, the sigmoid function, the rectifier function,
and we've got the hyperbolic tangent function.
In their raw forms, which ones would you be able to use for a binary variable?
cues.zh: 原始形式，哪些可用二元變數？

cues.en: Okay, so the answers here are, there's two options that we can approach this with.
So number one is the threshold activation function, because we know that it's between zero and one, and it gives you a zero under certain values, and then otherwise it gives you a one.
cues.zh: 第一閾值，因為只在 0、1，特定值以下給 0，否則 1。

cues.en: So it only can give you two values.
It fits perfectly, it fits this requirement perfectly.
And therefore you could just say y equals the threshold function of your weighted sum and that's it.
cues.zh: 所以 y 等於加權和的閾值函數，就好。

cues.en: And in the second case, what you could use is a sigmoid activation function.
It is actually also between zero and one, just what what we need.
But at the same time, you want just zero or one, right?
So it's not exactly what we need, but in this case, what you could use it as is the probability of y being yes or no.
cues.zh: 不完全符合，這時可作 y 是或否的機率。

cues.en: So we want y to be zero or one, but instead we'll say that the sigmoid function, sigmoid activation function tells us whether
cues.zh: 想要 y 為 0、1，但改說 Sigmoid 告訴我們，

cues.en: it tells us the probability of y being equal to one.
So basically, the closer you get to the top, the more likely it is that this is indeed a one or a yes rather than a no.
cues.zh: 越靠上，越可能是 1、是，而非否。

cues.en: And yeah, so that's very similar to the logistic regression approach.
And those are just two examples if you have a binary variable.
And now let's have a look at another practical application.
Let's have a look at how all this would play out if we had a neural natural like this.
So in the first input layer, we have some inputs.
They're sent off to our first hidden layer, and then an activation function is applied.
cues.zh: 送第一隱藏層，套活化函數。

cues.en: And usually what you would apply here and what you'll see throughout this course, is we would apply a rectifier activation function.
cues.zh: 通常這裡、課程也會看到，套整流活化函數。

cues.en: So it would look something like that.
We apply the rectifier activation function, and then from there the signals would be passed on to the output layer where the sigmoid activation function would be applied
cues.zh: 套整流，訊號傳輸出層，套 Sigmoid，

cues.en: and that would be our final output, and that could predict a probability, for instance.
cues.zh: 成為最終輸出，例如預測機率。

cues.en: So this combination is gonna be quite common, where in the hidden layers we apply the rectifier function, and then in the output layer we apply the sigmoid function.
cues.zh: 這組合很常見，隱藏層整流，輸出層 Sigmoid。

cues.en: So there we go. Hope you enjoyed today's tutorial.
Now you are quite well versed in the four different types of activation functions, and you will get some hands-on practical experience with them throughout this course.
cues.zh: 現在熟悉四種函數，課程會實際動手。

cues.en: We'll be using them all over the place, so you'll get to know them quite intimately and you should be quite comfortable with them.
cues.zh: 到處用，會很熟悉、很自在。

cues.en: But for now, this is the knowledge that you need to progress and understand what is going to be happening further down in this course.
cues.zh: 目前這些知識足以繼續，理解後續內容。

cues.en: And on that note, I look forward to seeing you next time.
Until then, enjoy deep learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
